title: Types of Insurance Regulated by IRDAI

cells: Provides financial support after death or retirement.

blocks.content: The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) is a statutory body formed under the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority Act, 1999.

rows: Protection against loss of life / Long-term investment
Indemnity against loss of property, asset, or health
Not applicable (Human life value cannot be precisely measured)
Strictly applicable (Compensation limited to actual loss)
Must exist at the time of policy inception
Must exist both at inception and at the time of loss (except Marine)

items: IRDAI was constituted based on the recommendations of the Malhotra Committee Report (1994).
Life insurance contracts are not contracts of strict indemnity, whereas general insurance contracts are strictly governed by the Principle of Indemnity.
Standard free-look period for offline policies is 15 days, whereas distance marketing/electronic policies carry a 30-day free-look period.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: IRDAI regulates both Life Insurance and General (Non-Life) Insurance sectors in India to ensure orderly growth and financial stability.
Life Insurance covers the risk of loss of life and functions primarily as a long-term savings and protection product.
General Insurance includes Motor, Health, Marine, Fire, and Property insurance, operating strictly on the Principle of Indemnity.
Health Insurance operates under specialized IRDAI regulations offering standalone coverages, family floaters, and critical illness policies.
Reinsurance operations, including domestic reinsurer GIC Re and foreign reinsurance branches (FRBs), are regulated by IRDAI.
